spec.description: PostgreSQL DB Overview - CPU, Memory, Disk, Settings, Connections, Locks. Metrics from postgres_exporter.

panels.description:
This panel gives a quick health overview of the PostgreSQL database pod.
If the value is Up (green), it means the database is running and responding normally.If it shows Down (red), it indicates the database is unavailable.
panels.title: Database Status

panels.description: This panel displays the total number of connections that are currently running queries. It indicates the workload on your database. A high number of active connections may suggest a heavy load on the server.
panels.title: Active Connections

panels.description: Remaining Connections panel shows how many database connections are still available before reaching the max connection limit.
panels.title: Remaining Connections

panels.description: This panel shows the maximum number of concurrent connections that your PostgreSQL database is configured to allow.
panels.title: Max Connections

panels.description: This panel shows the total number of connections that are currently open but aren't actively running any queries.
panels.title: Idle Connections

panels.description:
Measures the total rate of data blocks (8KB chunks) requested by queries per second.

    What it includes: Both blocks found in memory (cache hits) and blocks read from disk (physical reads).

    What it means: This is a direct measure of the total data access workload or "demand" on the database. A high value indicates the database is busy serving data.

    How to interpret: This panel is most useful when viewed alongside the Cache Hit Ratio. A high read rate with a high cache hit ratio (>99%) is healthy.
panels.title: Logical Block Reads/sec

panels.description:
This panel shows the percentage of database block reads that were served directly from memory (the cache) instead of from the disk.

A higher percentage indicates better performance, as retrieving data from memory is significantly faster than from disk.

targets.expr: pg_stat_database_blks_hit{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", rems_environment="$Env"} / (pg_stat_database_blks_read{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", rems_environment="$Env"} + pg_stat_database_blks_hit{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname"})

panels.title: Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: This panel shows the number of currently active sessions in the database. An active session is one that is currently running a query or is in a transaction.
panels.title: Active sessions

panels.description: This panel shows the total number of connections that are currently open but are not doing any work. This includes connections that are simply waiting for a new command and those that have started a transaction but are not actively running a query.

targets.expr: pg_stat_activity_count{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", state=~"idle|idle in transaction|idle in transaction (aborted)", rems_environment="$Env"}

panels.title: Idle sessions

panels.description: This panel shows the total number of rows that have been retrieved from the database by SELECT queries.
panels.title: Fetch data (SELECT)

panels.description: This panel displays the total number of rows that have been inserted into the database. A non-zero value indicates that new data is being added to the database tables.
panels.title: Insert data

panels.description:
Update Data
This panel shows the total number of rows that have been updated in the database.
panels.title: Update data

panels.description: This panel shows the total number of rows that have been returned by queries.
panels.title: Return data

panels.description: This panel shows the total number of rows that have been deleted from the database. A non-zero value indicates that rows are being permanently removed from your tables.
panels.title: Delete data

panels.description:
This panel shows the rate of transactions being processed by the database per second. It combines two key metrics:

Commits : The number of transactions successfully completed.

Rollbacks : The number of transactions that were aborted or failed
panels.title: Transactions

panels.description:
Measures the rate of rows (tuples) being modified by INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE commands per second.

    What it includes: The sum of all inserted, updated, and deleted rows across the database.

    What it means: This is a direct measure of the database's write workload, showing how frequently your applications are changing data.

    How to interpret: Spikes in this graph can directly correspond to application features, bulk data processing jobs, or high user activity. Consistently high values may indicate a write-intensive application.
panels.title: Tuples Modified/sec

panels.description: Tracks the time-based replication lag in seconds between the primary server and its replicas. High or consistently growing values can indicate network latency, high write load on the primary, or a replica struggling to keep up.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Replication Lag

panels.description: This panel shows the number of database locks that are currently active. Locks are mechanisms used by the database to manage concurrent access to data. A high or increasing number of locks, especially exclusive locks, could indicate contention, where multiple transactions are trying to access the same data at the same time, which can lead to performance bottlenecks and slow queries.
panels.title: Lock tables

panels.description: Provides a example to get more details of slow queries from the database.

options.content:
Pick a queryid you want to check details of from the top queries list.

1. Connect to PostgreSQL DB
2. Run Query for That queryid

```sql
SELECT queryid,
       query,
       calls,
       total_exec_time,
       rows,
       shared_blks_hit,
       shared_blks_read,
       shared_blks_dirtied,
       shared_blks_written
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE queryid = <copied_query_id>;
```

panels.title: Check Details of a Specific Query by queryid

panels.description: This panel identifies the top 50 SQL statements that have consumed the greatest cumulative execution time over the selected time range. It is designed to pinpoint queries contributing the most to the overall database load, based on metrics from pg_stat_statements. The 'Query' column shows the unique hash (queryid) for each statement, not the full SQL text. A negative queryid is a normal artifact of the hashing algorithm and has no special meaning.
panels.title: Top 50 Queries by Total Execution Time

panels.description: This panel identifies the top 50 I/O-intensive SQL statements by ranking them based on their cumulative block read time. It helps pinpoint queries that read the most data from disk instead of from memory cache, which is a common performance bottleneck. The ranking is based on metrics from pg_stat_statements. The 'Query' column shows the unique hash (queryid) for each statement, not the full SQL text. A negative queryid is a normal artifact of the hashing algorithm and has no special meaning.

targets.expr: topk(50, sum by (queryid, datname) (increase(pg_stat_statements_block_read_seconds_total{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", queryid=~"$queryid"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Top 50 I/O Intensive Queries (by Block Read Time)

panels.description: This panel identifies the top 50 SQL statements with the highest average execution time. The calculation divides the total time a query has run by its total number of calls over the selected time range, using data from pg_stat_statements. The 'Query' column shows the unique hash (queryid) for each statement, not the full SQL text. A negative queryid is a normal artifact of the hashing algorithm and has no special meaning.

targets.expr:
topk(50,
  sum by (queryid, datname) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", queryid=~"$queryid"}[12h]))
  /
  (sum by (queryid, datname) (increase(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{rems_application_group="$application_group", rems_service="$service", datname=~"$datname", queryid=~"$queryid"}[12h])) > 0)
)

panels.title: Top 50 Slowest Queries (by Avg Time)

panels.description: This panel shows the total memory allocated by PostgreSQL for the shared buffer pool. Shared buffers are used to cache frequently accessed data from tables and indexes to improve query performance.
panels.title: Shared Buffers (megabytes)

panels.description: This panel shows the amount of memory allocated by PostgreSQL for sorting and hashing operations within a single query. If a query requires more memory than this limit, PostgreSQL writes temporary data to disk, which can slow down query performance.
panels.title: Work Mem (megabytes)

panels.description: This panel shows the maximum size that PostgreSQL allows for Write-Ahead Log (WAL) files before triggering a checkpoint. If WAL usage reaches this limit, PostgreSQL performs a checkpoint to recycle old WAL files.
panels.title: Max WAL Size

panels.description: Shows the rate of index scans per second over a 5-minute window, helping monitor real-time index usage and query activity trends.
panels.title: Index Scan Rate per Schema

panels.description: Displays the number of rows fetched using index scans, grouped by schema in PostgreSQL. This metric helps evaluate how effectively indexes are used for retrieving data during query execution. Data is collected using postgres_exporter.
panels.title: Index Tuples Fetched per Schema

panels.description: “Shows the number of user tables present in each PostgreSQL schema.”
panels.title: Tables Count per Schema

panels.description: “How many useless (deleted/updated) rows are currently sitting in tables and waiting to be cleaned”
panels.title: Dead Tuples per Schema

panels.description: Displays the number of database connections per user and their current state (active, idle, etc.) across databases. Helps identify which users are actively running queries and which have idle or unused connections.
panels.title: User connection

panels.description: Shows the number of locks applied on database tables, grouped by lock type.
panels.title: Table lock

panels.description: Shows the number of row-level locks currently held in PostgreSQL, grouped by lock type and user.
panels.title: Row-based lock

spec.title: PostgreSQL
